mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a strong labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate is below 5% but the S&P 500 forward returns are not positive in more than 50% of the cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real GDP (GDPC1) at a rate exceeding 2% year-over-year indicates strong economic demand, which should translate to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth exceeds 2% YoY but the S&P 500 forward returns are not positive, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) at a rate exceeding 3% year-over-year indicates strong supply-side activity, which should lead to increased economic output and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth exceeds 3% YoY but the S&P 500 forward returns are not positive, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the 6-month moving average indicates a strong housing market, which should lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST is above the 6-month average but the S&P 500 forward returns are not positive, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increase simultaneously, it indicates potential inflationary pressures that may erode corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increase but the S&P 500 forward returns are positive, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) at a rate exceeding 0.2% month-over-month indicates a strong labor market, which should lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.2% MoM but the S&P 500 forward returns are not positive, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in retail sales (RSAFS) at a rate exceeding 4% year-over-year indicates strong consumer demand, which should lead to increased corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth exceeds 4% YoY but the S&P 500 forward returns are not positive, this hypothesis is rejected.
